title: Types of Sentences
content:
Definition

English: Sentences are classified based on their purpose or structure, expressing statements, questions, commands, or emotions.
Hindi: Vakya apne uddeshya ya sanrachna ke adhaar par vargikrit kiye jate hain, jo kathan, prashn, aadesh, ya bhavna vyakt karte hain.

There are four main types: Declarative, Interrogative, Imperative, Exclamatory.
Char mukhya prakar hote hain: Vivaranatmak, Prashnavachak, Aadeshvachak, Vismayadibodhak.

Example: Declarative: The sun rises. Interrogative: Does the sun rise? Imperative: Watch the sunrise. Exclamatory: What a beautiful sunrise!
Hindi: Vivaranatmak: Suraj ugta hai. Prashnavachak: Kya suraj ugta hai? Aadeshvachak: Suraj ka uday dekho. Vismayadibodhak: Kya sundar suryoday hai!

title: Declarative Sentences
content:
Definition

English: Declarative sentences express statements, facts, or information and convey a complete thought.
Hindi: Vivaranatmak vakya kathan, tathya, ya jankari vyakt karte hain aur ek poorn vichar prakat karte hain.

Use

Used to inform or state something.
Jankari dene ya kisi baat ko batane ke liye.

Structure

Subject + Verb + Object/Complement (if any)

Example: She reads books daily.
Hindi: Woh roz kitaabein padhti hai.

title: Interrogative Sentences
content:
Definition

English: Interrogative sentences ask questions to seek information or clarification.
Hindi: Prashnavachak vakya prashn puchhte hain jankari ya spashtikaran ke liye.

Use

Used to inquire or seek answers.
Poochhtachh ya jawab mangne ke liye.

Structure

Auxiliary Verb/Question Word + Subject + Main Verb + Object/Complement (if any)

Example: Where does he live?
Hindi: Woh kahan rehta hai?

title: Imperative Sentences
content:
Definition

English: Imperative sentences give commands, instructions, or requests.
Hindi: Aadeshvachak vakya aadesh, nirdesh, ya anurodh dete hain.

Use

Used to direct or request someone to do something.
Kisi ko kuch karne ka nirdesh ya anurodh karne ke liye.

Structure

Verb + Object/Complement (Subject 'you' is implied)

Example: Close the door.
Hindi: Darwaza band karo.

title: Exclamatory Sentences
content:
Definition

English: Exclamatory sentences express strong emotions, surprise, or excitement.
Hindi: Vismayadibodhak vakya tez bhavna, ashcharya, ya uttejana vyakt karte hain.

Use

Used to show intense feelings or reactions.
Teez bhavna ya prativikriya dikhane ke liye.

Structure

What/How + Adjective/Adverb + Subject + Verb OR Exclamation + Phrase

Example: What a lovely day!
Hindi: Kya sundar din hai!

title: Sentence Types Based on Structure
content:
Explanation

English: Sentences can also be classified by structure: Simple, Compound, Complex, and Compound-Complex.
Hindi: Vakya sanrachna ke adhaar par bhi vargikrit hote hain: Saral, Samyukt, Mishrit, aur Samyukt-Mishrit.

Types

  • Simple: One independent clause. Example: She sings.
    Hindi: Ek swatantra upvakya. Woh gaati hai.
  • Compound: Two or more independent clauses joined by conjunctions. Example: She sings, and he dances.
    Hindi: Do ya zyada swatantra upvakya samuchchay bodhak se jude. Woh gaati hai, aur woh narta hai.
  • Complex: One independent clause and at least one dependent clause. Example: She sings because she loves music.
    Hindi: Ek swatantra aur kam se kam ek ashrit upvakya. Woh gaati hai kyunki use sangeet pasand hai.
  • Compound-Complex: At least two independent clauses and one dependent clause. Example: She sings, and he dances because they love music.
    Hindi: Kam se kam do swatantra aur ek ashrit upvakya. Woh gaati hai, aur woh narta hai kyunki unhe sangeet pasand hai.
Example: Complex: When it rains, I stay inside.
Hindi: Jab baarish hoti hai, main andar rehta hoon.

title: Using Sentence Types Effectively
content:
Use

English: Different sentence types serve specific purposes: Declarative for information, Interrogative for questions, Imperative for commands, and Exclamatory for emotions.
Hindi: Alag-alag vakya prakar vishesh uddeshyon ke liye hote hain: Vivaranatmak jankari ke liye, Prashnavachak prashnon ke liye, Aadeshvachak aadesh ke liye, aur Vismayadibodhak bhavna ke liye.

Example: Declarative: The movie was great. Interrogative: Was the movie great? Imperative: Watch the movie. Exclamatory: What a great movie!
Hindi: Vivaranatmak: Film shandar thi. Prashnavachak: Kya film shandar thi? Aadeshvachak: Film dekho. Vismayadibodhak: Kya shandar film hai!
